title: Paired t test
biology: Plant physiologists measure photosynthesis in the same leaves before and after heat stress.
design: Twenty independent plants contribute one before/after pair each.
data_characteristics: Independent pairs; dependent observations within pairs
question: Is the mean within-plant change in photosynthesis zero?
null: The population mean of after minus before differences is zero.
options: Keep the same pair order in both vectors
First minus second determines the change sign
assumptions: Differences are roughly normal at small n
parametric: For multiple times use repeated-measures or mixed models
nonparametric: Sign test needs no symmetry but targets direction/median
practice: Would treating the before and after vectors as independent answer the design correctly?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1103)
before <- rnorm(20, 18, 2.2)
after <- before + rnorm(20, -1.3, 1.7)
d <- data.frame(plant = 1:20, before = before, after = after)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
matplot(1:2, t(as.matrix(d[c("before", "after")])), type = "l",
        lty = 1, col = "#00000033", xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
        ylab = expression(Photosynthesis~(mu*mol~CO[2]~m^{-2}~s^{-1})))
axis(1, 1:2, c("Before heat", "After heat"))
points(rep(1, nrow(d)), d$before, pch = 19, col = "#246A73")
points(rep(2, nrow(d)), d$after, pch = 19, col = "#B7663E")
code_analysis:
change <- d$after - d$before
fit <- t.test(d$after, d$before, paired = TRUE,
              alternative = "two.sided")
generating_model: 20 independent baseline values come from Normal(18, 2.2 SD). Each after value is its own baseline plus an independent Normal(-1.3, 1.7 SD) change.
generating_truth: The mean after-minus-before difference is -1.3 photosynthesis units, even if this sample provides limited evidence against zero.
teaching_point: A large p-value does not make the simulated nonzero effect disappear; paired differences define the target.
